name: Huaier (Trametes robiniophila mushroom)
short: Child ITP trial of a Huaier-goji-Polygonatum granule: severe events incl. low platelets, infection, bleeding (not split by group); overall events like placebo. Cancer add-on reviews: no excess.
text: In a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 216 children with chronic immune thrombocytopenia, a granule made mainly of Huaier, goji (Lycium chinense) and Polygonatum sibiricum was given for 24 weeks, then continued open-label, with follow-up for 96 weeks; adverse events and serious adverse events were comparable between the groups, and the severe adverse events reported included low platelets (6.9%), respiratory tract infection (5.1%) and bleeding episodes (2.8%) (the abstract does not split these by group). A meta-analysis of 14 randomized trials (885 children) of the same granule added to treatment for primary nephrotic syndrome found no significant difference in adverse events. For Huaier granule (an extract of the mushroom alone) added to conventional cancer treatment, a meta-analysis of 27 trials in 2562 people with breast cancer found less myelosuppression and liver toxicity with the granule and no significant difference in other adverse events, and a meta-analysis of 24 randomized trials (2664 people) in primary liver cancer reported fewer adverse reactions, with the evidence graded low to very low quality. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
